answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil farms with a one-time admission proof-of-work gate. Each new identity must mine a nonce so sha256(challenge:nonce) starts with a required count of leading zero bits; that proof is single-use and expires, and the difficulty rises whenever many joins arrive at once. A farm of N fake agents therefore pays roughly N times the hashing, with escalation making each extra head costlier. Like an umber beam split by a prism, one proof cannot be refracted into many identities, so the lagoon of rewards stays too shallow for a cheap army.
